summary: Two partners who share a courtyard and want to split it build a dividing wall right in the middle. Each one gives half of the land the wall stands on, and if the wall falls, the place and the stones belong to both.

chunks.en: Partners who want to make a dividing wall in their courtyard
chunks.st: Partners who wished to make a partition [meḥitza] in a jointly owned courtyard

chunks.en: build the wall in the middle.
chunks.st: build the wall for the partition in the middle of the courtyard.

chunks.en: In a place where people usually build with rough stones,
chunks.st: What is this wall fashioned from? In a place where it is customary to build such a wall with non-chiseled stone [gevil],

words.note: Stones that were not cut smooth.

chunks.en: or cut stones, or small bricks,
chunks.st: or chiseled stone [gazit], or small bricks [kefisin],

chunks.en: or large bricks, they build with that.
chunks.st: or large bricks [leveinim], they must build the wall with that material.

chunks.en: It all follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: Everything is in accordance with the regional custom.

chunks.en: With rough stones, this one gives three tefachim of land,
chunks.st: If they build the wall with non-chiseled stone, this partner provides three handbreadths of his portion of the courtyard

words.note: A tefach is about the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and that one gives three tefachim.
chunks.st: and that partner provides three handbreadths,
chunks.stMore: since the thickness of such a wall is six handbreadths.

chunks.en: With cut stones, this one gives two and a half tefachim,
chunks.st: If they build the wall with chiseled stone, this partner provides two and a half handbreadths

chunks.en: and that one gives two and a half tefachim.
chunks.st: and that partner provides two and a half handbreadths, since such a wall is five handbreadths thick.

chunks.en: With small bricks, this one gives two tefachim,
chunks.st: If they build the wall with small bricks, this one provides two handbreadths

chunks.en: and that one gives two tefachim.
chunks.st: and that one provides two handbreadths,
chunks.stMore: since the thickness of such a wall is four handbreadths.

chunks.en: With large bricks, this one gives one and a half tefachim,
chunks.st: If they build with large bricks, this one provides one and a half handbreadths

chunks.en: and that one gives one and a half tefachim.
chunks.st: and that one provides one and a half handbreadths,
chunks.stMore: since the thickness of such a wall is three handbreadths.

chunks.en: So if the wall falls down,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that

chunks.en: the place and the stones belong to both of them.
chunks.st: the space where the wall stood and the stones belong to both of them, to be divided equally.

summary: In a place where people usually fence off gardens, a neighbor must help build the fence. In open fields where people do not fence, one who wants a fence builds it on his own land and marks it as his.

chunks.en: And it is the same with a garden:
chunks.st: And similarly with regard to a garden,

chunks.en: where people usually build a fence, the neighbor must help.
chunks.st: in a place where it is customary to build a partition in the middle of a garden jointly owned by two people, and one of them wishes to build such a partition, the court obligates
chunks.stMore: his neighbor to join in building the partition.

chunks.en: But in open fields,
chunks.st: But with regard to an expanse of fields [babbika],

chunks.en: where people usually do not fence,
chunks.st: in a place where it is customary not to build a partition
chunks.stMore: between two people’s fields, and one person wishes to build a partition between his field and that of his neighbor,

chunks.en: the neighbor does not have to help.
chunks.st: the court does not obligate his neighbor to build such a partition.

chunks.en: But if one wants a fence, he moves in
chunks.st: Rather, if one person wishes to erect a partition,

chunks.en: onto his own land and builds it,
chunks.st: he must withdraw into his own field and build the partition there.

chunks.en: and he makes a mark on the outside.
chunks.explain: The mark shows that the wall is all his.
chunks.st: And he makes a border mark on the outer side
chunks.stMore: of the barrier facing his neighbor’s property, indicating that he built the entire structure of his own materials and on his own land.

chunks.en: So if the wall falls down,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that

chunks.en: the place and the stones are his.
chunks.st: the space where the wall stood and the stones belong only to him,
chunks.stMore: as is indicated by the mark on the wall. Nevertheless, in a place where it is not customary to build a partition between two people’s fields,

chunks.en: If they made it with both of them agreeing,
chunks.st: if they made such a partition with the agreement of the two of them,

chunks.en: they build the wall in the middle,
chunks.st: they build it in the middle, i.e., on the property line,

chunks.en: and make a mark on this side and on that side.
chunks.st: and make a border mark on the one side and on the other side.

chunks.en: So if the wall falls down,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the wall later falls, the assumption is that

chunks.en: the place and the stones belong to both of them.
chunks.st: the space where the wall stood and the stones belong to both of them, to be divided equally.

summary: If someone owns fields on three sides of his neighbor's field and fences them, the neighbor does not have to pay. Rabbi Yosei says that if he fences the fourth side too, the neighbor must share the cost of all of it.

chunks.en: If someone's fields go around his neighbor's field on three sides,
chunks.st: With regard to one who surrounds another on three sides,
chunks.stMore: that is, he owns parcels of land on three sides of the other person’s field,

chunks.en: and he fenced the first side,
chunks.st: and he built a partition on the first,

chunks.en: and the second and the third,
chunks.st: the second, and the third sides,

chunks.en: the neighbor does not have to pay.
chunks.st: the court does not obligate
chunks.stMore: the neighbor who owns the inner field to contribute to the construction of the partition if he does not wish to do so.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: If he went and fenced the fourth side too,
chunks.st: If he arose and built a partition on the fourth side of the field,

chunks.en: they make the neighbor pay his share of it all.
chunks.st: the court imposes upon the owner of the inner field the responsibility to pay his share for all of the partitions.

summary: If a courtyard wall shared by two neighbors falls, each must help rebuild it up to four amos high. If one later builds on the taller part, he must pay his share of all of it.

chunks.en: A shared courtyard wall that fell down:
chunks.st: In the case of a dividing wall in a jointly owned courtyard that fell,

chunks.he: מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ לִבְנוֹתוֹ עַד אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: they make each neighbor help build it up to four amos high.
chunks.st: if one of the owners wishes to rebuild the wall, the court obligates the other owner to build the wall with him up to a height of four cubits.
chunks.stMore: If after the wall was built one of the neighbors claims he alone constructed it and the other did not participate in its building, the latter is nevertheless

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm, from elbow to fingertip.

chunks.en: We assume he already gave his share,
chunks.st: presumed to have given his share of the money,

chunks.en: unless the other brings proof that he did not give.
chunks.st: unless the claimant brings proof that the other did not give his part.

chunks.he: מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה, אֵין מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: Higher than four amos, they do not make him help.
chunks.st: The court does not obligate the reluctant neighbor to contribute to the building of the wall higher than four cubits.

chunks.en: But if he built another wall up against it,
chunks.st: But if the reluctant neighbor built another wall close to the wall that had been built higher than four cubits, in order to set a roof over the room that was thereby created, the court imposes upon him the responsibility to pay his share for all of the rebuilt wall,

chunks.en: even though he has not
chunks.st: even though he has not yet

chunks.en: yet put a roof on it,
chunks.st: set a roof over it.

chunks.en: they make him pay his share for all of it.
chunks.explain: He showed he wants to use the tall wall.
chunks.st: Since he has demonstrated his desire to make use of what his neighbor built, he must participate in the cost of its construction. If the builder of the first wall later claims that he did not receive payment from his neighbor, the neighbor

chunks.en: Here we assume he did not give his share,
chunks.st: is presumed not to have given his share of the money,

chunks.en: unless he brings proof that he did give.
chunks.st: unless he brings proof that he did in fact give money for the building of the wall.

summary: People who share a courtyard can make each other help pay for a gatehouse and a door, and people in a city can make each other help pay for a city wall. Someone counts as a person of the city after twelve months, or right away if he buys a house there.

chunks.en: They can make each neighbor help build
chunks.st: The residents of a courtyard can compel each inhabitant of that courtyard to financially participate in the building of a

chunks.en: a gatehouse and a door for the courtyard.
chunks.st: gatehouse and a door to the jointly owned courtyard.

words.note: A little room at the gate for a guard.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees and says:

words.note: A title for the head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.he: לֹא כָל הַחֲצֵרוֹת רְאוּיוֹת לְבֵית שָׁעַר.
chunks.en: Not every courtyard needs a gatehouse.
chunks.st: Not all courtyards require a gatehouse,
chunks.stMore: and each courtyard must be considered on its own in accordance with its specific needs. Similarly, the residents of a city

chunks.en: They can make each person help build
chunks.st: can compel each inhabitant of that city to contribute to the building of

chunks.en: for the city a wall, doors, and a bolt.
chunks.st: a wall, double doors, and a crossbar for the city.

words.note: A bar that locks the doors shut.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees and says:

chunks.en: Not every town needs a wall.
chunks.st: Not all towns require a wall.

chunks.he: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בָעִיר וִיהֵא כְאַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר,
chunks.en: How long must someone be in the city to count as one of its people?
chunks.st: With regard to this latter obligation, the mishna asks: How long must one live in the city to be considered like one of the people of the city
chunks.stMore: and therefore obligated to contribute to these expenses?

chunks.en: Twelve months.
chunks.st: Twelve months.

chunks.en: If he bought a house to live in there,
chunks.st: But if he bought himself a residence in the city,

chunks.en: he is like the people of the city right away.
chunks.st: he is immediately considered like one of the people of the city.

summary: Partners can only make each other split a shared courtyard, field, garden or building if each part is still big enough to be used and keep its name. If both want to split, they may, but they may never cut up a holy scroll.

chunks.en: We do not split a shared courtyard
chunks.st: The court does not divide a courtyard at the request of one of the joint owners

chunks.en: unless there will be four amos
chunks.st: unless there will be in it four by four cubits

chunks.en: for this one and four amos for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and four by four cubits for that one,
chunks.stMore: i.e., this minimum area for each of the joint owners.

chunks.en: And not a field,
chunks.st: And the court does not divide a jointly owned field

chunks.en: unless it has room to plant nine kav of seed
chunks.st: unless there is space in it to plant nine kav of seed

words.note: A kav is a measure of seed or grain.

chunks.en: for this one and nine kav for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and nine kav of seed for that one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The court does not divide a field

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָהּ תִּשְׁעַת חֲצָאֵי קַבִּין
chunks.en: unless it has room for nine half-kav
chunks.st: unless there is space in it to plant nine half-kav of seed

chunks.en: for this one and nine half-kav for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and nine half-kav of seed for that one.

chunks.en: And not a garden,
chunks.st: And the court does not divide a jointly owned garden

chunks.en: unless it has room for half a kav
chunks.st: unless there is space in it to plant a half-kav of seed

chunks.en: for this one and half a kav for that one.
chunks.st: for this one and a half-kav of seed for that one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says
chunks.stMore: that half that amount is sufficient, i.e., the

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: room to plant a quarter kav is enough.
chunks.st: area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed [beit rova].

chunks.en: And we do not split a big hall,
chunks.st: Similarly, the court does not divide a hall [hateraklin],

chunks.en: and not a sitting room,
chunks.st: a drawing room,

chunks.en: and not a dovecote,
chunks.st: a dovecote,

chunks.en: and not a cloak,
chunks.st: a cloak,

chunks.en: and not a bathhouse,
chunks.st: a bathhouse,

chunks.en: and not an olive press,
chunks.st: an olive press, and an irrigated field

words.note: A place where olives are squeezed for oil.

chunks.en: unless there is enough
chunks.st: unless there is enough for this one to use the property in the usual manner

chunks.en: for this one and enough for that one.
chunks.st: and enough for that one to use the property in the usual manner.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Anything that can be split and still keep its name, we split.
chunks.st: Anything for which when it is divided, each of the parts is large enough to retain the name of the original item, the court divides it.

chunks.en: And if not, we do not split it.
chunks.st: But if the parts will not retain the original name, the court does not divide it.

chunks.en: When is this? When they do not both want to.
chunks.st: When does this rule apply? It applies when the joint owners do not both wish
chunks.stMore: to divide the item; when only one of the owners wishes to divide the property, he cannot force the other to do so.

chunks.en: But when both of them want,
chunks.st: But when both of them wish to divide the item,

chunks.en: even with less than this, they may split it.
chunks.st: they may divide it, even if each of the owners will receive less than the amounts specified above.

chunks.en: But holy scrolls,
chunks.st: But in the case of sacred writings,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a scroll of any of the twenty-four books of the Bible, that were inherited by two people,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם רוֹצִים, לֹא יַחֲלֹקוּ:
chunks.en: even if both of them want, they may not split them.
chunks.st: they may not divide them, even if both of them wish
